name: Which San Diego Kitchen Renovation Work Requires a Permit?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for a kitchen remodel in San Diego if I keep the cabinets in the same layout?
mainEntity.text: Do I need a permit for a kitchen remodel in San Diego if I keep the cabinets in the same layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keeping the same cabinet layout does not automatically eliminate permitting. A project may still require approval if it adds electrical circuits, changes gas piping, relocates plumbing, modifies walls, upgrades ventilation, or changes structural openings. Replacing cabinets and countertops in the same locations is often simpler, but the exact scope and local rules control. Ask the contractor for a written permit determination before work begins. The property address matters because San Diego, Chula Vista, Coronado, National City, Imperial Beach, and other cities may use different departments, forms, fees, and review procedures. Clarify whether the contractor or homeowner submits plans, schedules inspections, and pays fees. Do not rely solely on a verbal statement that a permit is unnecessary. Unpermitted work can complicate inspections, insurance questions, resale disclosures, and future remodeling. Keep approved plans, inspection records, product information, and final sign-off documents. If the scope changes after demolition, pause and confirm whether revised plans or additional inspections are required.
acceptedAnswer.description: Cosmetic work such as painting, hardware replacement, cabinet refacing, and some same-location fixture changes may not require a permit. Permits are commonly needed when work changes plumbing, gas lines, electrical circuits, walls, windows, doors, or ventilation. Confirm requirements with the applicable city before demolition because rules can differ by jurisdiction.
